title: Capstone: The Support Prompt Pack
objective: After this lesson you will be able to ship a complete, measured prompt pack (system prompt, few-shot set, output contracts, eval gold set with scores, guardrails, and budget accounting) for a support assistant — the portfolio artifact this course builds toward and the on-ramp to the RAG/agent courses.
why: Courses end with artifacts, not chapters: a prompt pack is shippable, reviewable, and improvable — and it plugs directly into LangGraph/CrewAI/RAG courses as the reasoning core inside agents. This walkthrough performs the full assembly once, with numbers, so your capstone project repeats it on your own domain.

blocks.text: The pack: six components, one version

A **prompt pack v1.0** contains: (1) system prompt (identity, scope rules, refusal shapes, abstention path); (2) few-shot set (coverage-audited, one negative, hardest last); (3) output contracts per stage (classify/decide/draft JSON); (4) gold eval set (15 items: 6 happy, 6 edge, 3 attacks) with baseline scores; (5) guardrails (triage router, scope sentences, logging); (6) budget sheet (tokens/call, monthly projection). Versioned together — prompts, examples, and evals change as one unit, never separately.

blocks.code:
PACK v1.0 — shoe-store returns triage (illustrative numbers)
 system: identity + 30-day/receipt/final-sale policy + scope-to-POLICY + unknown-path
 few-shot: 4 pairs (billing/shipping/returns/damaged-edge) + lateness negative
 contracts: classify {category, confidence} / decide {approved, reason} / draft ≤60w
 gold: 15 items (6 happy, 6 edge, 3 attacks) — baseline 12/15 (0.80)
 guardrails: triage router + refusal shapes + attempt logging
 budget: ~1,100 tokens/call ≈ $0.0055 → ~$165/mo at 1k calls/day
blocks.caption: Six components, one version number, measured baseline

blocks.text: Build sequence with gates: system + contracts first (Ch.1–3) → few-shots to fix observed misses (Ch.4, added for measured gaps, not upfront bulk) → guardrails (Ch.6) → gold set + baseline score (Ch.7) → budget sheet (Ch.8) → failure-mode review (Ch.9: which modes own gold items?). Each step's output feeds the next; the baseline score (12/15) is the number every future iteration must beat on the same set.

Deliver findings like the SQL capstones: what the baseline shows (3 misses: 2 edge confusions, 1 attack slip), what each miss teaches (which lesson's fix), what ships now vs next (negatives added, trigram-equivalent deferred prompt work), and the honesty section (abstention rate, refusal log summary, calibration note). Measured, cited, improvable — the artifact that gets you hired or promoted, not just graded.

blocks.title: Score the pack baseline
blocks.note: Run it: expect 12/15 overall, edge 4/6, attack 2/3. Per-kind breakdowns (not just the headline) direct the next iteration: edges need examples, the attack needs guardrails.

items: Pack = system + few-shots + contracts + gold/scores + guardrails + budget, versioned as one unit
Build in gate order; baseline everything on the same set; improve single variables
Memo: misses with lessons, ship-now vs next, honesty section — measured and improvable

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the baseline scorer and state which kind needs examples vs guardrails. (b) Draft your capstone domain (not shoes): the four-part system prompt skeleton with your policy facts. (c) List your 15 gold items by kind with one-line expectations each (not full text — the plan, graded on coverage thinking).
hints: Edges 4/6 → few-shot examples (boundary teaching); attack 2/3 → guardrails (scope/triage). Per-kind scores prescribe different fixes — that prescription is the skill.
System skeleton: identity + scope sentences + abstention path + refusal shapes; policy facts from YOUR domain (library fines? course refunds?).
Gold plan: 6 happy (core behaviors), 6 edge (boundaries + negatives), 3 attacks (injection, scope-push, confusion) — each with expected behavior, not prose.
exercise.why: Per-kind prescription (examples vs guardrails by failure kind) is triage applied to evaluation — the capstone's planning skill. Domain transfer (shoes → yours) proves the method travels.

quiz.q: Baseline 12/15 with edge 4/6, attack 2/3. Next iteration priorities?
options: Edge examples for boundary misses + guardrail work for the attack slip — per-kind scores prescribe different fixes
quiz.explain: Per-kind breakdowns direct iteration: edges need teaching (examples), attacks need defense (scope/triage). Aggregate-only views prescribe nothing.

quiz.q: Teammate edits few-shots without re-running evals. Risk?
options: Unmeasured drift: pack components version together; example changes need same-set re-scoring or regressions hide
quiz.explain: Version-as-unit discipline: prompts, examples, evals change together with recorded scores. Silent example edits are unmeasured bets.

quiz.q: This pack feeds a RAG agent next. What transfers directly?
options: Contracts, eval gold sets, guardrails, and budget sheets plug into agent nodes; retrieval supplies the context slot the pack already structures
quiz.explain: The pack is agent infrastructure: node prompts reuse contracts/evals, guardrails wrap tool calls, budgets scale per retrieved context. Prompt engineering compounds into agent engineering.

summary: Six components, one version, gated build order, per-kind iteration, honest memo. The pack is shippable, improvable, and agent-ready — course complete, assessment next.
